AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should broken glass be kept out of compost? (1 mark)
   A. It rots too fast
   B. It smells bad
   C. It does not rot and can cut people
   D. It makes the heap too wet

2. Which sign shows that compost is ready? (1 mark)
   A. It is hot and full of whole peelings
   B. It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
   C. It is wet and smells sour
   D. It is grey and hard

3. Where is the best place to make a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   B. In the middle of a stream
   C. In a very windy open road
   D. Inside the kitchen

4. What does soil conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Selling soil to other farmers
   B. Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   C. Digging up all the soil on a farm
   D. Covering the soil with plastic

5. What should you do if a hole in a drip pipe is blocked? (1 mark)
   A. Throw away the whole system
   B. Cut the pipe in half
   C. Clear it gently with a thin wire
   D. Pour hot oil in it

6. Who should make holes in bottle caps and pipes with a nail? (1 mark)
   A. A small child alone
   B. Anyone with wet hands
   C. A teacher or an adult
   D. Nobody

7. Where is the neck of the bottle placed in a bottle drip system? (1 mark)
   A. In the bucket
   B. High in a tree
   C. On the leaves
   D. In the soil beside the plant

8. Which of these is a part of a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A container for water
   B. A tractor
   C. A scarecrow
   D. A compost heap

9. What is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. A cleaning tool
   B. A kind of food
   C. A type of soil
   D. Something we burn to get heat

10. What is a good first step if a person's clothes catch fire? (1 mark)
   A. Wave the arms
   B. Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   C. Run fast
   D. Jump in the air

11. Why do children need an adult when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Fuels and fire can burn people
   B. Children cannot lift a spoon
   C. Adults always cook faster
   D. Fire is not dangerous

12. Which is a problem of cutting many trees for firewood? (1 mark)
   A. More rain falls at once
   B. Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   C. The soil becomes richer
   D. Trees grow faster

13. Why do we use more than one method of scaring animals? (1 mark)
   A. It confuses farmers
   B. Animals can get used to one method
   C. One method is always cheaper
   D. It uses more soil

14. Which animal is a domestic animal, not a wild one? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Hare
   C. Squirrel
   D. Monkey

15. What is biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Only wild plants
   B. The variety of living things on Earth
   C. A type of crop
   D. Only birds

16. Which is the safest way to make holes or dig for scarecrow parts? (1 mark)
   A. Use broken glass
   B. Ask an adult to help
   C. Use bare hands on sharp tools
   D. Play with the tools

17. Which crop can be harvested about four to six weeks after sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Radish
   B. Mango
   C. Millet
   D. Banana

18. Why should tiny seeds not be sown deeply? (1 mark)
   A. They become large
   B. They grow faster
   C. They wash away
   D. They run out of stored food before reaching the light

19. What is thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Adding more seeds
   B. Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   C. Cutting all plants
   D. Making soil thin

20. Why do we cover the seeds with a thin layer of fine soil? (1 mark)
   A. To make them bigger
   B. To stop them growing
   C. To protect them and keep them moist
   D. To let birds find them

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how to sow tiny seeds in a drill. (4 marks)

22. Write the steps for growing carrots from seed to harvest. (5 marks)

23. What is meant by coexisting with wild animals? (2 marks)

24. A school wants to make compost from kitchen and garden wastes. Write a plan with the materials, the place, the steps and the safety measures. (5 marks)

25. A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use. (5 marks)

26. Name three small wild animals that destroy crops. (3 marks)

27. Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking. (2 marks)

28. Name two materials that can be used to make compost. (2 marks)

29. Give two reasons why soil should be conserved. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It does not rot and can cut people
   Glass never rots and can injure anyone handling the compost.

2. B — It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
   Ready compost looks and smells like soil and the materials cannot be recognised.

3. A — A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   A shaded, dry spot protects the heap from sun and flooding.

4. B — Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   Soil conservation protects the soil from being washed away and from losing its plant food.

5. C — Clear it gently with a thin wire
   A thin wire clears blockages without damaging the pipe.

6. C — A teacher or an adult
   Nails and awls are sharp and can cause injuries.

7. D — In the soil beside the plant
   The bottle is buried neck down near the plant.

8. A — A container for water
   A container holds water for the pipe or bottle.

9. D — Something we burn to get heat
   Fuels such as wood and gas are burnt for heat.

10. B — Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   Rolling smothers the flames.

11. A — Fuels and fire can burn people
   Adults can guide and help prevent accidents.

12. B — Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   Trees protect soil and water, so cutting them harms the environment.

13. B — Animals can get used to one method
   A mix of methods works better.

14. A — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

15. B — The variety of living things on Earth
   Biodiversity includes all the different animals and plants.

16. B — Ask an adult to help
   Safety comes first.

17. A — Radish
   Radish grows very quickly.

18. D — They run out of stored food before reaching the light
   Deep seeds cannot push up to the surface.

19. B — Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   Thinning gives strong plants space.

20. C — To protect them and keep them moist
   Covering helps seeds germinate.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a shallow drill about 1 cm deep; mix seeds with sand; sprinkle thinly in the drill; cover lightly with fine soil; water gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare a fine seedbed; make drills about 1 cm deep; sow seeds thinly with sand; cover and water gently; thin to about 5 cm; weed and water; harvest after three to four months by loosening the soil and pulling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Living together peacefully so that both farmers and animals are safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for living together, 1 mark for both safe.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: peelings, leaves, grass. Place: shaded, well-drained, near the garden. Steps: sticks, layers, water, cover, turn. Safety: gloves, wash hands, keep children away from the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 for place, 2 for steps, 1 for safety.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct animal.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Vegetable peelings, dry leaves, grass, straw or animal dung (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Soil grows our food, and if it is washed away or made poor the crops will fail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soil grows food, 1 mark for erosion or loss of plant food.
